headline: Local AI Gives VFX Artists Control, Frame by Frame
lede: The promise of AI-generated video has long collided with a practical problem for professionals: cloud services charge per second and offer limited creative precision. Mick Mahler, a German VFX educator known online as mickmumpitz, has published a free workflow that runs entirely on a local GPU, compositing AI-generated footage directly into real video using an open-source stack.
body:
The pipeline stitches together two open-source video models that compensate for each other’s weaknesses. **SkyReels V3** (in its *R2V*, or reference-to-video, mode) is a 14-billion-parameter model that anchors the visual identity of a subject — a face, an object, a costume — consistently across frames. Wan *VACE* (Video-Aware Composable Editing), developed by Alibaba (BABA) and released under an Apache 2.0 open-source licence, handles spatial guidance: it accepts masks, *ControlNet* signals, and *inpainting* instructions that define which region of the footage to replace and what geometry to respect. Together they solve what neither does alone — SkyReels knows who is in the shot; VACE knows where that person sits in space.

ControlNet, a conditioning framework invented by Lvmin Zhang and Maneesh Agrawala in 2023, is what makes the approach practically useful for compositing work. A *depth map* — a greyscale image where brightness encodes distance from the camera — guides the AI to fill a masked area while obeying the scene’s three-dimensional structure. Edge-detection and pose-estimation maps work similarly. The result is a generated patch that reads as plausible footage rather than a floating hallucination.

The whole stack runs inside *ComfyUI*, a node-based inference engine created by an anonymous developer known only as “comfyanonymous” and launched in January 2023. ComfyUI exposes every step of the *diffusion* computation as a wirable node — load model, apply ControlNet, sample, decode — rather than hiding the pipeline behind a polished button. Workflow files are plain JSON; only changed nodes re-execute between runs; output is compatible with Nuke, After Effects, and DaVinci Resolve via *EXR* export. The project has passed 89,000 GitHub stars and was voted the single most important tool for VFX artists to learn in a 2026 industry poll.

The timing is pointed. OpenAI shut down Sora in April 2026. Cloud alternatives remain metered: Kling, made by Kuaishou (1024.HK), charges roughly $0.07 per second of generated video; Runway’s plans start at $15 per month with additional compute costs on top. For a VFX artist running a hundred takes to nail one clean composite, those charges accumulate fast. The underlying open-source model — Wan2.1, from Alibaba — runs free on a consumer GPU with as little as 8GB of VRAM, carries no content restrictions, and scored 86.22 on *VBench*, a standard video-quality benchmark, compared to Sora’s 84.28 when it was active.

Mahler is not a hobbyist packaging tutorials on the side. He holds a degree from the *ifs Internationale Filmschule Köln* and a Fulbright scholarship to study at the Savannah College of Art and Design; he now lectures in a professional AI-in-media programme at ifs and tutors at *HFF München* (Hochschule für Fernsehen und Film). His YouTube channel has passed 100,000 subscribers, and the Patreon community tied to this video grew by 196 percent in thirty days — a signal that demand is coming from working professionals, not casual experimenters.

concepts.definition: A video-generation mode in which the model is given a still image as a reference and tasked with producing footage that preserves the visual identity — face, object, costume — of the subject shown. Unlike text-only generation, R2V constrains the output to remain on-model across all frames, solving the “character drift” problem common in AI video.

An open-source, node-based interface for running AI diffusion models locally. Users connect processing nodes — model loaders, samplers, ControlNet applicators — into a directed graph that makes every step of the generation process explicit and editable. Released in January 2023 by an anonymous developer known as comfyanonymous; now maintained by Comfy Org with more than 89,000 GitHub stars.

A conditioning framework for diffusion models, introduced by Lvmin Zhang and Maneesh Agrawala in 2023, that adds spatial guidance to image or video generation. Instead of steering output with text alone, ControlNet accepts auxiliary visual inputs — depth maps, edge-detection images, pose skeletons — and uses them to constrain the model’s spatial decisions frame by frame.

An open-source video-editing module developed as part of Alibaba’s Wan model family. VACE accepts text, reference images, masks, and ControlNet signals simultaneously, allowing a user to define which region of footage to replace and what structural constraints the replacement must satisfy. Available in 1.3B-parameter and 14B-parameter variants.

A technique in which a masked region of an image or video frame is filled by an AI model, generating new pixels that plausibly match the surrounding context. In VFX work, inpainting is used to remove objects from a scene, extend backgrounds, or replace elements with AI-generated content.

A greyscale image in which pixel brightness encodes distance from the camera — bright for near, dark for far, or vice versa. In AI video compositing, depth maps are fed to ControlNet to ensure generated content respects the three-dimensional geometry of the original scene rather than floating unconvincingly in space.

A class of generative AI model that learns to produce images or video by iteratively denoising a signal starting from random noise. Most contemporary AI image and video generators — Stable Diffusion, Wan, and the now-discontinued Sora — are built on diffusion principles.

A high-dynamic-range image file format developed by Industrial Light & Magic and maintained by the Academy Software Foundation. It supports multiple image layers and float-precision colour data, making it the professional standard for exchanging compositing elements between tools such as Nuke, After Effects, and DaVinci Resolve.

A video-generation benchmark suite developed at Nanyang Technological University that evaluates AI video models across dimensions including subject consistency, motion quality, background stability, and aesthetic score. Results are reported as a percentage out of 100; higher is better. Wan2.1 scored 86.22, above the 84.28 recorded for OpenAI’s Sora.

repos.summary: The main repository for ComfyUI, the open-source node-based interface for running Stable Diffusion and other diffusion models locally. Users build workflows by connecting processing nodes into a directed acyclic graph; workflow files are JSON and can be embedded in generated images for full reproducibility. With over 89,000 GitHub stars it is the de-facto standard for customisable local image and video generation.

The official repository for Wan2.1, Alibaba’s open-source video generation model released under Apache 2.0. The model comes in 1.3B and 14B parameter variants, runs on consumer GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM, and includes the VACE module for masked, ControlNet-guided video editing. It scored 86.22 on VBench, above the 84.28 recorded for OpenAI’s Sora while that model was active.
